title: A Machine Learning Model for Predicting In-Hospital Mortality in Chinese Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Findings From the China Myocardial Infarction Registry.
summary: Machine-learning prediction on China Myocardial Infarction Registry data identified factors and estimated in-hospital mortality risk after ST-elevation myocardial infarction; conclusions are registry-specific.
ai_technology: XGBoost models use CAMI registry variables to estimate in-hospital mortality after ST-elevation myocardial infarction; SHAP interprets predictors.
organization: State Key Laboratory of Cardiovascular Disease

evidence.tested: Trained on 9,616 CAMI patients, the model achieved AUC 0.896 in a CAMI validation set and 0.840 in the independent China PEACE cohort, compared with lower GRACE/TIMI AUCs.
evidence.unknown: Registry-based evaluation is retrospective; cross-cohort prediction does not establish prospective impact on patient management.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost models use CAMI registry variables to estimate in-hospital mortality after ST-elevation myocardial infarction; SHAP interprets predictors.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
